utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody. Is the next witness ready? Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. He is. Good afternoon to you, good afternoon, Your Honours, and everyone. The next witness is ready, Mr. President. However, before bringing him into the courtroom I had indicated or asked to make a preliminary application in two respects. First is that, given this witness's involvement in the events concerning the Skorpions execution video that you've seen, I would ask for him to be given a caution pursuant to Rule 90(E) of our rules. The second is, having met with him for the first time a little earlier this morning, he indicated for the first time that he would like protective measures in respect of his testimony. The extent of the protective measures he seeks is face distortion and not a pseudonym, and -- if we can go into private session, please, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the record, we are back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now, please rise and stand for a moment, sir. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card which is shown to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And please sit down again. I think before the Prosecution starts with the examination-in-chief, I would like to give you some guidance about your position and your rights. Rule 90(E) of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence has a paragraph which I would like to read out for you. I quote: "A witness may object to making any statement which might tend to incriminate the witness. The Chamber may, however, compel the witness to answer the question. Testimony compelled in this way shall not be used as evidence in subsequent prosecution against the witness for any offence other than false testimony." Sir, did you understand what I was reading to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, I suppose, Mr. Prosecutor, Mr. Vanderpuye, has some questions for you. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Indeed I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Stojkovic. We didn't receive a translation of his answer. I think he said good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters could not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I am going to ask you to try to keep your voice up and allow a moment between the question and your answer so that the interpreters can both hear you and have an adequate opportunity to translate what you say and what I say so that it's clear for everyone in the courtroom. Did you understand that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now in July 1995 were you a member of the so-called Skorpions Unit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how long had you been a member of this unit prior to that time?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: From 1991 -- or, rather, I joined in May 1992, and I was a member of the Skorpion Unit since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In July 1995, where was this unit based?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: It was based at Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Where was its headquarters?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: The command was at Djeletovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us about how many members comprised this unit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: You mean all the members or only those who were out in the field?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All of the members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on page 9, line 6, the witness mentioned the name of the place but it wasn't properly recorded, so I kindly ask the Prosecutor to clarify. It is only for the sake of the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Gajic is right. I heard another name.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I am not sure whether Mr. Gajic is referring to Trnovo, which I see in the transcript, or Djeletovci, which I see in the transcript at line 6. Maybe that's the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if that's the case, can you tell us where the unit was headquartered.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, now, I don't quite understand the question. You mean the headquarters in the field or the headquarters where we were founded, where we worked, and functioned? So I need additional explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The headquarters were you worked and where you were founded, where you set out from.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: The name of that place is Djeletovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And where is that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Today it's in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Where was it then, in 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: In 1995 there was the Republic of Serb Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I interrupt for a moment. I don't know how to explain that in English. It is not better yet, but even worse. I quite clearly heard the name Djeletovci. Can you please repeat the name of this village. Is it Djeletovci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Djeletovci, D -- It is not Deletovci but Djeletovci, D-J-E-L-E-T-O-V-C-I.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's remark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It is again not recorded correctly. Can you -- I am very sorry, can you repeat that very slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Djeletovci. In our language it isn't written with an initial "Dj," but the initial letter is Dz.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Which doesn't exist in the English alphabet, interpreter's remark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And now I would like to ask you to repeat the name very slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Djeletovci.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: There is a problem there, Mr. President, that I think the witness's last answer to you was not recorded in the transcript, despite all our efforts. So I think if we just have him spell it into the record, that might be the most efficient way to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So if you could, just spell the name into the record. And use your alphabet so we record it correctly.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I've already said: Djeletovci. The initial letter is "Dj."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. You indicated that Djeletovci was in the Republic of Serb Krajina in 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I asked you approximately, if you can tell us, how many members the Skorpions Unit had in 1995. There is -- that includes the members in the field and also the members in the headquarters in Djeletovci.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: About 230 to 250.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in 1995 was your unit provided with uniforms and other identifying insignia indicating that you were members of the Skorpions Unit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: We became members of the Skorpions in 1994. The name goes back to that year. We received uniforms, military insignia, a military post number.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just so that we can be clear in the record, the uniforms that you received, can you just briefly describe them, and then describe the military insignia and the military post number, if you can tell us what that is, or was, as long as you can recall that.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember what the military post number was. I forgot it. And as for the uniforms, they were black overalls with insignia on the shoulders. We had Skorpion insignia, and we also wore berets, black or red ones. We were issued both colours. And the commanders wore American uniforms which were not overalls. They were green.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Were you issued identification cards or anything of that nature in order to identify yourselves as members of the unit as well?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you recall what the identification cards provided? What did they say?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Those were regular ID cards, just like the military booklets, the military IDs in former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sorry for interrupting you. I would like to ask one question. You said, sir, that you were wearing black overalls with insignia on the shoulders. "We had Skorpion insignia." You said "on the shoulders." On both shoulders? On both upper arms? And if yes, were they identical?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they were identical and on both sleeves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In 1995 can you tell us what your regular responsibility was within the unit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: In the Skorpions I was active in logistics, comprising the cafeteria and the kitchen for the soldiers. I was head of the kitchen and I was also in charge of some supplies; that is, food. This was my job. I was responsible for supplies.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And before this period of time, that is, before July of 1995, did you occupy any other position within this unit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could you tell us what that position or what those positions were?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I was head of a reconnaissance unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how long did you perform that particular duty in the unit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Almost two years. Or maybe a year and a half. I don't remember precisely, but not longer than two years.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In July 1995, who was in command of the Skorpions Unit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Slobodan Medic, also known as Boca.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And had he been in command of the unit since you joined it in 1992, I think you've indicated?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And who was the unit's second in command or deputy commander?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Aleksandar Vukov was deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And had he been in that position since you joined the unit as well?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, not during that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was he the deputy commander in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I want to ask you about some other members of this unit. Are you familiar with Branislav Medic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was he a member of the unit in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with Aleksandar Medic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was he also a member of the unit in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Before I go on, let me ask you, Branislav Medic, what was his position within the unit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: He was a driver and he also maintained vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What about Aleksandar Medic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Aleksandar Medic was a member of the commander's security detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Slobodan Davidovic, do you know who he is?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was he also a member of the unit in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What was his position?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: He was a member of the commander's security detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with Milorad Momic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was he also a member of the unit in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what was his position?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: The commander's security detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know who Pera Petrasevic is?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was he also a member of the unit in 1995 and a member of the commander's security detail?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In 1995, aside from Trnovo, as you've indicated, was the unit assigned to any other locations in Bosnia or Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No other location in 1995 apart from Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With respect to your assignment to the Trnovo area, can you tell us when you received this assignment to go there?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it was about a week before departure. It was in July 1995. I don't remember the exact date. I don't quite remember when we got the news, but I know that during the last days I went off to procure food. We procured our own food and we had to take care to obtain some.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you procure this food in advance or in anticipation of the assignment to go to Trnovo in particular?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know precisely where we were going, but I had a superior who knew some things that I didn't. But I did know that I had two or three days to procure food for a certain number of soldiers. I know -- or, rather, I knew how many soldiers were supposed to go and then I knew exactly how much food was required so they have enough when they set off.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How many soldiers were supposed to go?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, 120 or 130. I cannot be sure as to the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the unit or that number of soldiers being sent to the Trnovo area?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. You will have to ask the commander. To my understanding, they were supposed to hold the line there, at Trnovo. Nothing else, as far as I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you say "hold the line," do you mean participate in combat operations in that area?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, certainly there would be combat in case of an attack from the enemy, but we were not an assault unit. We were a defensive unit. That's why we did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I take it that in participating in holding the line, that your unit was expected to work in conjunction with the armed forces of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that would be in co-ordination with the Army of Republika Srpska, the VRS?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And also the MUP of the Republika Srpska; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that aspect. I can't answer that question because I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recall who you heard the information from regarding the assignment to go to Trnovo? You mentioned a superior; can you tell us who that is?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I did have a superior. It was Branislav Vucenovic who was my immediate superior, and there was also Slobodan Medic, Boca, but it was from him that I got direct instructions as to what I should do and what preparations should be made.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: From "him" meaning Vucenovic or from "him" meaning Boca?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Vucenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, do you recall the trip that the unit made to Trnovo in any detail?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't really remember all the details because I was very busy during those two days. I had a lot of work procuring food so that I spoke -- slept from Djeletovci to Bijeljina. I don't know what happened during that time, but I woke up at Bijeljina and I drove a refrigerator truck all the way to Pale -- well, no, it isn't Pale. What's the name of the place, the skiing centre on Mount Jahorina, next to the Sator Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, I would like to ask you a little bit about how the unit got from Djeletovci to Jahorina. Was it transported in trucks, buses, other kinds of vehicles? Can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, there were both trucks and buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you indicated that you slept until the unit arrived in Bijeljina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So you don't know the specific route that the unit took to get from Djeletovci to Bijeljina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And Bijeljina at the time would be in Bosnia, right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You mentioned that you drove a truck from Bijeljina to Jahorina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how many people were in the truck that you drove?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: The two of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Meaning whom?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Me and Branislav Vucenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what was it that you were transporting in your truck?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Food.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recall the route that you took to get from Bijeljina to Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that we travelled through Zvornik and Han Pijesak, Pale, and from Pale we went up to Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I take it that in driving this truck through these areas, Zvornik, Han Pijesak, Pale, and ultimately Jahorina, you passed through a number of check-points?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't notice any.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So you were never stopped by any army or MUP within the Republika Srpska in order to transport this food in your truck and, as well, the other soldiers within your unit through to Jahorina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Not as far as I know. That may have been the case, but I was in the rear, at the end of the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I see. So you were never provided with any papers or documents to present in case the convoy were to be inspected by officials of Republika Srpska, meaning the army or the MUP.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: They didn't stop me and I don't see why they should have. But, anyway, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Were you provided with a plan or a route of the convoy before your departure from either Djeletovci or Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I was just in the convoy. That was enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, you've indicated that you passed through Zvornik, Han Pijesak, Pale, and Jahorina. Did you stop in all of those places before you arrived in Jahorina, or anyplace else?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, we didn't stop anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you stop in Jahorina for any amount of time?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of stopping in Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that we spent a day or two at Jahorina. I am not sure, but it was at least one day. We spent the night there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And what was the purpose of stopping in Jahorina? I take it that you were on your way to Trnovo, right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: About the purpose, I don't know, but I know that on the following day we set off for Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter 7003 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I am showing you is an entry in the 20 April 2007 judgement of the Belgrade Court, the War Crimes Chamber. And just bear with me a moment, I will give you the page number.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: But I think we will need page 55 in English and page 45 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What you should have in front of you is some of that Trial Chamber's findings concerning the Defence of the accused in that case, Branislav Medic. And what I would like to refer you to is, in the English, it's about halfway through the long paragraph on that page, and it reads as follows, and maybe I can orient you to it. It reads: "They took the weapons from Djeletovci, except for smaller ammunition, and everything else they needed they obtained in Trnovo from the military command of the Bosnian units, and the Maljutkas, bombs, mortar shells, and other items they brought from Jahorina. You should find that in the paragraph in the top of the page in the B/C/S, just after where you can see, I think, the number 150. Does that comport with your recollection of what transpired while you were in Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this detail is not familiar to me, that we picked up this ammunition, because we had our own ammunition, we had our own mortars with us, and as far as I know we did not pick up anything there other than bread.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall or do you know if members of your unit had any contact with members of the VRS, the Army of Republika Srpska, or MUP officials of the Republika Srpska while you were in Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know about that part. Maybe they did, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you hear about anything like that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know. I was more in the logistics part, so I really don't know what they discussed. I did hear that he went to meet the commander, but what they discussed I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You heard that who went to meet the commander, and which commander?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, my commander, Slobodan Medic, attended some meetings, but whom he met with or what they discussed, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: He attended meetings while you were in Jahorina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know anything about that. He may have, but I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Fair enough. But is that what you heard?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can remember, no, there was no mention of any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell us about how all the circumstances under which you set out, your unit set out, from Trnovo -- I mean, from Jahorina to Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I am not sure I understand your question. What do you mean under what circumstances, or what the circumstances were?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you leave with the same number of individuals that were in Jahorina? Did they go to Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, they did not all go to Trnovo. Some of them remained at Hotel Sator at Jahorina, some six men or so, and also a trailer-truck remained there. There was some foodstuff left in the truck, the things we couldn't fit in the refrigerator truck, but there was also ammunition there and everything that we needed for the unit, including fuel. And whatever the unit had, whatever materiel they had, they took with them, and we then also went to Hotel Sator where we would take things we needed and replenish our assets.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How many people went from Jahorina to Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly the number, but at least 120 men. I just know for certain that six people remained behind at Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know why they remained behind in Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, all I know is that this trailer-truck was left there with the materiel that was needed for replenishment, so somebody had to stay there with that. In other words, buses, the trailer-truck, and their drivers remained there, and a number of men who had to guard those buses and trailer-trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell us about how far it was from Jahorina to Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, at the time, we took the path through the woods. I couldn't tell you exactly how far it was then, but it took us about three hours to get there. Now, in kilometres, I really wouldn't know how far that was, but I know that we set out at night. So I really can't guess now what the kilometres -- how far it was in terms of kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you arrived in Trnovo, can you tell us, did you or members of your unit have any contact with VRS officers or MUP officials there? MUP officials meaning of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I did not have any contacts with anyone. There was no need for that. Those who did have the need probably had their contacts, because it was logical to expect that the commander would have to meet with someone to talk about where to put up the men and so on, because how else would he have known because he had never been there before.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know who the commander met with to talk about these specific issues?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Would they have been officers of the Bosnian Army or of the -- I should say the VRS, or of the Republika Srpska MUP?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know who he met with. He certainly did meet with some people, but who it was I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I see we still have 65 ter 7003 in e-court. We are at page 35.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I read to you a portion of it a moment ago, and in particular I read to you a part of this document which mentions that, and with respect to weapons, that everything else needed was obtained in Trnovo from the military command of the Bosnian units. Do you have any information concerning the obtaining of ammunition or weapons from the Bosnian units, meaning the VRS or the MUP, in the Trnovo area?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, there was no need for us to obtain any ammunition there because we had the ammunition we took with us. Now, that may have been the case, but I don't know anything about it. But as far as I know, we did not get or weren't issued anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I want to take you a little bit further down the page, and it's about two sentences from where I left off, where it reads: "When they arrived in Trnovo, the commander went to a meeting with Bosnian officers ..." Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. He may have gone to meet someone, but I really can't recall. He probably did have a conversation with someone, but I really don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just a suggestion: Perhaps the Prosecutor can clarify with the witness, or, rather, what portion of the decision, judgement, he is reading from. Perhaps we can then see whether these were the words of a witness or whether these were the findings of that particular court. So perhaps he can clarify that, for the purpose of the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That would be helpful for a better understanding, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, and I do appreciate that, and I think I actually have done it but I will do it again. These relate to the judgements, findings, or assessment of the defence of the accused of Branislav Medic. It is designated 6.5 in this document. And so this is what the Trial Chamber in that case has assessed of the evidence that was given in respect of that defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So I have asked you whether you are familiar with these circumstances, not with the words of the judgement or the findings of the judgement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And which line is it you are referring to in the B/C/S and the English? I don't find it at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I can't tell you the exact line. I can tell you that it's in the first paragraph in the B/C/S, it's about three-quarters or two-thirds into that paragraph. In the English, it's exactly in the middle of the paragraph that is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yeah. If you -- maybe it will be helpful to indicate -- it's immediately preceded by the number 30. So if you can find number 30 in there and you will see the exact entry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So I have asked you, Mr. Stojkovic, whether you are familiar with the commander having gone to a meeting with Bosnian officers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic is on his feet. Please let him announce his comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my apologies for interrupting again, you know I don't like to do that and do not resort to it very often, but perhaps the Prosecutor can further clarify. I believe it is only as of page 48 of this judgement that the facts are laid out, whereas the portion which is now being put to the witness is, in fact, a short summary of the witness's words and testimony before this Court. Perhaps I can also find the exact spot, but you can clearly see that the facts are established only in portion 7 of the judgement, which begins at page 48.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is not my testimony or my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: Of course. We are referring here to the accused who were the accused in the case before the Belgrade Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I appreciate the comment from my friend Mr. Gajic, although I don't think it has any relevance in terms of the issues I have put to the witness because I'm asking the witness not about the veracity or accuracy of any findings or any statement of anyone else, I am asking him specifically whether he has familiarity with the circumstances that are indicated in this document, and that's a pretty simple question: He either does or he doesn't. I don't think whether it's the words of a witness, the findings of a judgement, or some other person's statement that has any bearing on whether or not he's familiar with the circumstances that are recounted. So I will put my question again, which is:

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the circumstances that are recounted in this document about a meeting between the commander, which I assume is Boca, and Bosnian officers when your unit arrived in Trnovo in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. It may have been the case, but I don't know anything about it. I did not have such information available to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me take you to page 85 in English, and it should be page 65 in the B/C/S. I think this one may be a little bit easier to find. I believe this area relates to the findings of the Court, but I am sure my colleague Mr. Gajic will correct me if that's incorrect. Nevertheless, in the italicised part of this document on page 65, it reads that: "After going to Republika Srpska, to the area of Trnovo, the 'Skorpioni' Unit was on the combat line in the zone of responsibility of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps of the Army of Republika Srpska." First, Mr. Stojkovic, are you aware of this and does this comport with your recollection of the events concerning the unit -- your Skorpions Unit that was assigned to that area?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is where our unit was deployed, but now I am hearing also for the first time what that area was known as, the name of it. I didn't even know what it was called.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And you see, in the next line, it says: "The head of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps at that time was General Milosevic." Did you know that at the time or have you learned that since?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know then nor do I know now. It was irrelevant to me who the commander was there; I knew who my commander was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. In the following paragraph, it reads that: "From the moment they came to the Trnovo area, the 'Skorpioni' Unit was, as the Court had established on the basis of the testimony of the witness Milanovic, acting pursuant to the orders of the Army of Republika Srpska corps commander, in this concrete case, General Milosevic. From what it could be concluded that in that area it did not have any connections with the home corps and was exclusively under the commander either of a corps or a brigade in that zone of responsibility." Per your memory and experience, was it the case that the Skorpion Unit was under the command of a corps or brigade in the area or zone of responsibility in which you found yourselves in the area of Trnovo in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't have that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Would it have been the case that a combat unit, such as yours, travelling from Krajina, the Serbian Republic of Krajina, into Bosnia to participate in operations there would fall under the command of a military or MUP unit in that area?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that is probably how it should work. Whether that was indeed the case, I really, in this particular instance, I don't know. The commander should really -- the unit commander should be the one to tell you about it because I didn't know. I had nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let me just go over to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's page 6 -- I'm sorry, just a moment. It should be page 86 in the English, and I think we will stay on page 65 in the B/C/S. And we may have to go over the page if it's not correct. This relates to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, this segment I am about to read you to relates to the testimony of witness Tomislav Kovac --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you turn to this part, may I put a question to the witness. Your commander, Slobodan Medic, aka Boca, from whom did he receive orders during this operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whom he received his orders from. Probably from someone. But since I was in the rear part, I couldn't -- I wasn't privy to that information nor do I know whom he met with or got his orders from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vanderpuye -- another question from Judge Mindua.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Witness. To follow up on what the Presiding Judge has just put to you, you said that you did not know who was giving orders to your commander, and I am talking about Slobodan Medic, aka Boca, so that's for one. But within your unit, I was wondering whether you would talk with other members of your unit, with other commanders about Slobodan Medic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... mean did we talk with them? We've been on speaking terms since I was a kid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have not received the French interpretation. Could we ask the witness to repeat the answer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your last answer. We had a problem with the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the commander and I have known each other from since we were born. I was born in 1965 and he 1966. We lived in the same town. We always sat together, chatted, had coffee, and so on and so on. If I had any time off, we were there together, but I could never ask him where he was going or whom he had talked with, nor did I care about it, frankly speaking, because we received our orders from him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And indeed since you were playing cards with him and you were talking to him every now and again, I was wondering whether your commander would touch upon the difficulty of his mission, the positive sides of it, or instructions coming from his superiors. Did he not talk at all to his subordinates? Did he not talk to his colleagues?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He probably did but I was not one of that circle of subordinates. I was in the logistics section, and I was only there when they talked about some event to be organised. But as to what was happening and what was to be done, I don't know anything about that. I just know that on one occasion I was punished and sent to the front line where I actually just -- because I had been sunbathing earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you for your answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, would you agree that it would be a good time for the first break?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We must have our first break now. The Court Usher will assist you during the break and we will resume 20 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. All right. I think I was on page 86 of the -- page 86 of the judgement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In the English, that's right. Thank you, Mr. President. And I was referring the witness to the testimony that was attributed to Tomislav Kovac. If we can go to the next page in the English -- I'm sorry, we were on the right page to begin with. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At the bottom of the first paragraph, it reads that: "He was informed when this unit arrived at their camp at Jahorina and that an order was issued that they may spend a night there after which they were to set off to Trnovo where they were to report to the tactical group commander, Ljubisa Borovcanin."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It should be page 66 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Ljubisa Borovcanin, of course, was the commander of the special police brigade of the Republika Srpska Ministry of the Interior, of the MUP. Tomislav Kovac was heading that ministry at the time. Were you aware of the responsibility of your unit, or the obligation of your unit, to report to Ljubisa Borovcanin in the area of Trnovo in July of 1995, Mr. Stojkovic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you know if your unit or the command of your unit did, in fact, report to Mr. Borovcanin in and around that time?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that detail. He may have, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we read a little bit further down this page we will see further evidence is attributed to Mr. Kovac. Right at the top of the second paragraph, in the English, and I think it's the same in the B/C/S, it says: "From the testimony of the witness Tomislav Kovac, it was also established that the entire Trnovo theater of war, that is the army which fought on that territory, was organised by the principle of municipal brigades. Starting from such an organisation, the tactical orders to the unit 'Skorpioni' were issued by the commander of the brigade in that zone of responsibility, and that was Lieutenant-Colonel Sehovac." Do you have any recollection or information with respect to the tactical orders that were received by your unit with respect to responsibilities it was to carry out in the Trnovo theater of war in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I know nothing about what you're saying. I don't know the people you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So you have no information that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We hear a strange sound in our earphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is it possible that you try to use the other microphone? Perhaps there is some interference with the microphones of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I am not sure, Mr. President. I have heard the -- the feedback is the sound that you are hearing, even when my microphone has been off, so I am not sure. I will try a different microphone. Maybe it's better now. No, I still hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I was told it has something to do with the earphones and the microphones used by the witness. Perhaps it will be better now. Please carry on, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now you have two microphones on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The Lieutenant-Colonel Sehovac that's referred to here, and maybe you can see this in the document in front of you, it refers to a Goran Sehovac, was the commander of a light infantry brigade, 2nd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade, in that area. Now, it's your information, Mr. Stojkovic -- well, is it your testimony that you don't have any information concerning how or the manner in which tactical orders were issued to your unit during the period of time that you were in the Trnovo area?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know these people, and I also don't know what kind of tactical orders were issued to my commander. I was not informed of these things. He probably did have orders, but those orders did not reach me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would like to take you to the time that you were in Trnovo. During the period of time that you were there, what were your ordinary responsibilities? Were they still to tend to the issues concerning the food and other logistic matters?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I was only in charge of food there. I did nothing else nor did I have other responsibilities. I had the problem that I had to go to the front line for one day and that was punishment because I had been sunbathing for a day before that. I had to take pictures of one section that -- I received an order to that effect, and that's the only thing I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You say -- well, what's been transcribed as "take pictures." Now do you mean by that using a video camera to record certain events?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I used a video camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: During the period of time that you were in Trnovo, can you tell us where the command in the field was set up for your unit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean "where"? The command was outside Trnovo, and we all stayed in some weekend cottages, about a kilometre and a half in the direction of Foca. Those houses were on a hill. That's where we were billeted. There were weekend cottages, some of which were devastated, but others were in good condition, and that's where we found accommodation and lived there, basically.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you say "we," do you mean the entire unit or just parts or some of the unit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: The entire unit; that is, all of us who were there. But we weren't all in those weekend cottages at the same time. Half of us were at the front line and the other half were resting.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You mentioned that you were called upon at a certain point to use a video recorder and to record the events, or some events, that occurred while you were in Trnovo. Can you tell us how that came about?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Here's how it happened: Dusko Kosanovic had a camera before me, and he accompanied the unit and all he did was record. But then he had some psychological problems. He was returned to Djeletovci, probably couldn't bear everything that was happening there, and the camera stayed behind, whereas he went to Djeletovci. When he left, the commander gave me the camera, and when there is a convenient moment or when I had leisure time, that I should go and take footage, and that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So when did the commander tell you to take footage in your leisure time? Was that soon after you arrived, some days after?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember when exactly it was and all the details, but once Kosanovic left, I took over the camera. When I had free time I could go and use it. I only had to report that -- what I was up to.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last part of his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If you could just repeat the last part of your answer. I think the interpreters were not able to catch what you said.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to say that in my free time I could use the camera but I had to report to the commander and tell him where I wanted to go and what I wanted to record. I couldn't just go off on my own without telling anybody anything. I mean when I took footage of irrelevant things.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What kind of footage did you take while the camera was in your possession?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I took footage at the front line. I took footage of fighters, the enemy forces, where their positions were. I can't remember everything because it was long ago. I'd have to look at all the footage and I don't have it. That would remind me of all the things that I recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you received the assignment, if it was an assignment, to use the camera, was -- were you given any specific directions on what types of things to film, when to film, or how to film?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't receive any instructions, nor was I issued the camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know somebody by the name of Djuro Opacic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us about him?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean? I know that he was a driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did he show you how to operate the camera?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, I misunderstood. You mean -- you probably mean Djuro Opacic, also known as Coke.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Did Coke teach you how to use the camera, or show you how to use the camera?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I take it that was before you went out, using it to film things in the area of Trnovo, where you were deployed.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, not before. Until that time, I did not use that camera. It was issued to Dusko Kosanovic and he filmed things where he went. It wasn't me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Understood. And when you got the camera, did Coke show you how to use it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you remember anything in particular about the camera, such as what type of camera it was or what type of film or media it used to record?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: The media was video casettes, the regular kind. And it was a Panasonic M6 or M7. One of the two, I am not sure which.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was among the things that you filmed during the period of time that you had the camera the execution of six Bosniaks in and around the area of Trnovo in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And were you asked or ordered specifically to film this execution?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was ordered.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Who ordered you to?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: The commander, Slobodan Medic, personally ordered me to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you record this execution, Mr. Stojkovic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you knew about the men who were executed and that you recorded.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I knew nothing about them. On that morning they woke me up and I was ordered to go and record. While we were going there, to the site where they would be executed, I learned that they were from Srebrenica. Whether they really were, I don't know, but that's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you, Mr. Stojkovic, participate in questioning these men about where they came from?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't participate, but I didn't know where they were from, and I wanted to ask Pero Petrovic [as interpreted] or whoever, I don't know, about them so that we should know where they were from, how old they were, and so on, but I was unsuccessful. That was not recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You are recorded in the transcript as having said or having mentioned a Pero Petrovic. Did you mean a Pera Petrasevic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Pera Petrasevic, yes, that's who I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I want to show you 65 ter 7003 again.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We need to go to page 29 in English and page 28 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: As was the case before, this refers to the judgement which recounts the defence of Pera Petrasevic. You can see your name in the, should be the second paragraph on the B/C/S page, I think.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At the end of the paragraph in the English, close to the end. It reads: "In the meantime, Slobodan Stojkovic kept on insisting that the detainees should be talked to in order for them to find out who they were and where they were from, and for that reason he squatted down and talked to them, and that was when the accused -" Pera Petrasevic - "found out for the first time that they were from Srebrenica, that the oldest was born in 1959 and the youngest in 1979." Does that accord with your recollection, Mr. Stojkovic, of your conduct with respect to these six Bosniak men?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as I see, this is Pera Petrasevic's statement that he gave at the trial, but I couldn't squat down beside them because if I had done so, I wouldn't have been able to film. So I was in no position to approach them and ask them questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when did you learn that these men were from Srebrenica, and under what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: When we left the cottage houses for the execution site, as I didn't know where they were from, I asked myself who they were or where they were from and what is going on, and the driver was Medic. And I was sitting next to him, and I asked him who these people were, and he said they were from Srebrenica. I said that's impossible. I know that Srebrenica was almost 200 kilometres away. How could they be here? That's what went through my head. When we arrived at the site, it occurred to me that we could ask the people themselves who they were and where they were from, but there was no opportunity to ask them that. I thought that they were bragging when they were saying that they were from Srebrenica and I didn't believe that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what have you learned since then, Mr. Stojkovic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: What exactly do you mean? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you learn subsequently that these men were, in fact, from Srebrenica, from either members of your unit or from other sources?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't learn where they were from until the trial before the special court in Belgrade, because the execution was very short and nobody subsequently asked questions, who they were, where they were from, and so on. Nobody cared. Other problems arose and things remained as they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you hear that these men were brought to the area of Trnovo by a bus?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, you didn't hear that, or no, you don't know that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear and I don't know either.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can I have, please, in e-court, P1397. We will have to go to about page 18, I think, in the English, and it should be page 27 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I am showing you, sir, is a statement that you gave to Belgrade District Court Investigating Judge by the name of Milan Dilparic on 15 June, 2005. Do you remember giving a statement to that investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I remember I did. I don't know exactly what I said, but basically it was what you asked me about today.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And what I am referring you to in particular is, and maybe this will refresh your recollection, in the middle of the page in English you can see the judge asks you: "Did you hearing anything about it later, about how they came to your unit?" meaning the men that were executed. And your answer was: "I only heard that they were brought by truck. Well, now, how, what, where from ..." And he asks you: "Did you hear who drove them?" And you said: "I cannot say that since I don't know that." Does that refresh your recollection as to what you heard about how these individuals were brought from Srebrenica to Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it does. It does actually reflect what I said then. And I believe that my answer was almost identical here; in other words, that I do not know how they arrived there, if I understood your question correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, who did you receive information from that they were brought there by truck?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't really know. As I sit here I can't recall who it was who told me. It was probably being rumored that that's how they had been brought, but I really don't know the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I want to take you to page 23 of this same statement. And it should be page 35, hopefully, in the B/C/S. And you will see there the investigating judge asks you the following question, which is: "We will make conclusions. Tell me, since you were present, you're still saying that you were far from the place while the six of them were being interrogated on the way down. Did those people say where they were from, who they were, anything about that?" And your answer was: "I received information that they were from Srebrenica. Now, whether the information is true or not, I can't ..." I presume you were about to say you can't say. Now, what I would like to ask you about in particular, and maybe this has refreshed your recollection, is what is the information that you received about them being from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would appreciate it if we could be pointed to the page and line number, and also if the witness can be referred to the section, because as it is now, I am unable to follow this, and perhaps the witness will also find it easier to answer the question if he is shown the exact portion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Vanderpuye, is that the right page in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I am going to double-check it. It should be page 35 in the B/C/S. And as you can see, it's hard for me to read it, it's in Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: At the moment we are on page 34.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, then it should be page 35 in the B/C/S. The document page 35, e-court page 36, I understand, but you should see, on the bottom of the screen, 35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have that on the screen, and I hope it's the right one.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. We will try again.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you see the part of the - and you will let me know, Mr. Stojkovic - do you see the part where the investigative judge says, "We will make conclusions"? Can you find that on this page? Maybe General Tolimir can help us out here, too.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye. That part does not appear on the B/C/S that we have on the screen now. Neither I nor my legal assistant were able to find it, and the witness is unable to do so as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Then let's try the previous page, 34. It's missing a page, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It should be now the right page, if we are not mistaken. No, we have seen that already.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: It is in the last paragraph on page 34 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, it seems to be that the last answer and the question on the bottom of the B/C/S page seem to be the same as those when the witness said: "I don't remember any way he came, and as far as I remember and as much ..." and so on. Is that the relevant part?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The last paragraph on page 34 mentions the conclusions that the investigating judge would draw and then what -- how far that was, how far the witness was. So perhaps it follows on, on the next page. Perhaps the witness can be shown that portion, too, and then we can see if it's there.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The paragraph before last seems to be the one starting with "I can't remember ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we have it now clear on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And now we have the wrong page for sure. It's the following page, and it follows the paragraph where the witness says, "I don't remember ..." Whatever the next page may be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, that paragraph is on the screen, and now we have the next part that should be, "I received information."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you see here where the investigating judge says: "We will make conclusions"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, it is on the previous page in B/C/S. It's the last paragraph on the previous page, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you see that, Mr. Stojkovic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you can see the question that he asks you, which is: "Tell me, since you were present --" and maybe General Tolimir can tell me if the translation is accurate too -- "you were still saying that you were far from the place while the six of them were being interrogated on the way down. Did those people say where they were from, who they were, anything about that?" Do you see that on the page in front of you, Mr. Stojkovic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can we identify, for the record, whether it's the second to last or the last paragraph on this page.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: It's the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, please, so that we can look at your answer. Do you see your answer on the top of the next page, Mr. Stojkovic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is your answer: "I received information that they were from Srebrenica. Now, whether the information is true or not, I can't ..." And it discontinues at that point.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recall giving that answer to that question by the Investigating Judge Dilparic on 15 June 2002?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was your answer in reference to the six Bosnian men that you filmed being executed in the area of Trnovo in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what I want to ask you is, the information that you say that you received about these men, what was that information and where did that information come from?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: That is information that I learned on the way to the execution site, and I heard them -- I heard it from Branislav Medic, but as I already said here, I did not really believe that they were from Srebrenica and I didn't because he had said that they were from Srebrenica, and that is why I insisted, once we got off the truck, while I was trying to replace the battery, to have someone ask them where they were from so we could establish that. And up to this day, I really don't know whether they were or weren't from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did anyone ask them where they were from?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that. They were supposed to ask them, but then I think they changed their mind. Why? That also I don't know, but I seem to recall that they weren't asked where they were from.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the information you had concerning their transportation there by truck, and I say "truck" in particular because that's what you mention in your statement, where did you get that information from and when did you get it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I've just told you now that was while we were on the way, driving there. I think it was 100 -- a TAM-110 or -150 truck, so on the way to the execution site, which was of some 4 to 5 kilometres, that's when I heard it. Now, when I got there, I asked Branko where these men were from and he said they were from Srebrenica, and I had them ask them, and then I didn't believe them that they were from Srebrenica when they said so because I thought that maybe they were just trying to show off, because how could they get all the way from Srebrenica to this particular place?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would like to show you P1372. And we will need to go to paragraph 105. I have it as page 19 in the English. And if it's any help, that's very near the end of the document altogether, so it should be a page or two back, maybe two pages back in the B/C/S, from the last page. I understand it's page 25 in the B/C/S, and we've got it. Okay. In this paragraph, the witness mentions: "A few days after the fall of the enclave, I was at Treskavica." First of all, can you tell us where Treskavica is, Mr. Stojkovic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Treskavica is near Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Would that be near the area where your unit had set up, in that area in Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Further on, we see that the witness says: "When I went to see him, meaning Boca, I saw a bus full of civilians arrive, escorted by the CSB. These were civilians from Srebrenica. The CSB people called Boca out and removed the civilians from the bus. Boca asked what was going on, and he was told that these civilians were 'our share.' The CSB man explained to them that they were distributing civilians for killing in different locations because they didn't want too many killed in one place." Do you see that written in the statement in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you have any of this information?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, no. And the gentleman who said this, he probably worked for one of those institutions and that's why he would have that information. He was probably the commander's right hand, the man just next to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, it would be helpful if you could state for the record which statement or from whom this statement was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I will, Mr. President. And I was just going to ask him one other question and then I plan to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Beneath this section that I have just read to you, it says that the CSB man -- oh, I have read that part, I'm sorry. "Boca had these people locked up. He told six men, including Miodrag Momic and Slobodan Stojkovic, aka Bugar --" First of all, can you tell me, do you go by the name or have you gone by the name "Bugar"?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: He told six men, including Momic and Stojkovic, to get shovels so that it would appear to the Muslims that they were being asked to do some work. Do you have any -- does this comport with your recollection of the events?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, this is a fabrication.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Do you know somebody by the name of Goran Stoparic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How do you know him?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I know him from the unit. I was his superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was he a member of the unit in 1995, July?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was he assigned with your unit to the area of Trnovo in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Have you discussed the events of what you recorded in Trnovo with Mr. Stoparic prior to coming here to testify today, in any respect?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I've lost touch with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. What I've shown you, therefore, is a statement of his from November of 2003.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I haven't seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I would like to show you -- I take it, then, that you deny that you had any contact or information about these Srebrenica men or taking up shovels or anything that he's mentioned in his statement, at least in that paragraph, that concerns you. You deny that, right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, obviously, since I didn't do these things. This man provided a statement who wasn't even there on the spot, so how could he have known? He just was not in a position to see anything like that or to know so much about it. However, if he was employed by some sort of security service of Serbia, that's possible. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you say "security service of Serbia," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't have any specific opinion. It's just that if this man has this kind of information and he was just a simple soldier, how would he have known, unless he had some sort of position? And I could not really observe that when I knew him at the time, that he did have any of the authorities that would go with it. I think this is something quite different.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, you do see in the paragraph 105 that I've read some of, that he says that Bugar took a camera and filmed the people, meaning the people that were shot, that these Muslim civilians were lined up and shot in groups. And he says, "I saw the video of these people being killed." You see that, right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it is accurate that you were the person that filmed these people being shot, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it is true that they were lined up, as you can see in the video footage. Does that comport with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean they were lined up? I am not sure I understood what you said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would appreciate Mr. Vanderpuye's being more precise in his question. He said that people were killed in groups, that they had gotten off buses, that this was at Treskavica, and now he's talking about the murders in Trnovo. So let's just clear up what they are talking about -- or what he's talking about, because Treskavica is a mountaintop. Because this way it appears as if the witness is avoiding and not willing to answer the questions truthfully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, Mr. Vanderpuye is quoting from a statement of another person, of Mr. Goran Stoparic, obviously, and I don't see any mistake by putting some parts of these statements, of these sentences, to the witness. Please carry on, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You said you had a question about --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: May I add something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it was unclear to me, too, where it says there, you know, getting off the bus, then he took out his video camera and then filmed it, which would appear to be suggest that there was a whole busload of people and that they were all killed, but that was not the case. We know that there were six people, and this was a TAM-110 or -150 truck that these people were taken in there. I don't know where this information came from and I don't know how this person could have known what was happening some 4 kilometres further beyond that place. Perhaps he is clairvoyant or something, I don't know. In any case, this does not comport with what I filmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It does not comport with what you filmed; is that right? I just want to make sure the record is accurate in that sense.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, all right. Well, we will take a look at some of what you filmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could have P12 -- I'm sorry, just a moment. P102 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I don't want to disturb your line of questions, but perhaps you can clarify the relation between the different locations mentioned in paragraph 105.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Meaning Treskavica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
