utterances.text: Can you tell us where Treskavica is relative to where it was that these executions that you filmed took place? How far away is it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean where our unit was in relation to the execution site? Is that what you're asking?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: More specifically, since there is a reference to Treskavica, can you tell us, first of all, of what significance is that location to your unit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I am confused again. I haven't understood your question. Do you mean how far was the execution from the front line or how far our unit was or -- I really don't know what you want me to answer, what question you want me to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe I can frame it this way: Where Mr. Stoparic says, "I was at Treskavica," do you know where that is?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And does Treskavica have some relationship to where your unit was either billeted or headquartered during the period of time it was in Trnovo or in the Trnovo area?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, clearly the command and the place where we were billeted and the front line, that was some 4 to 5 kilometres off in the -- on the mountaintop, up the hill, and the line, the front line, was some 4 to 5 kilometres. We were there, our commander was there; that's how I remember it, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: "There" meaning at Treskavica?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And so the reference here by Mr. Stoparic to, "I was at Treskavica" means the area where the command was, of the unit. Is that a fair assumption?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, no, that's not a fair assumption. The command was in Trnovo, some one and a half kilometres away from Trnovo, where the cottage, the summer cottage was. As for the front line and the unit, they were in the hills -- up the hills some 4 to 5 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How far was Treskavica, then, from the command of the unit in Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I have just told you, 4 to 5 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what's there? Why would he be there, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I am not sure I understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: As a member of the unit, why would a member of your unit be in Treskavica when the command and where everybody else is billeted is someplace else? If you know.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's how we operated. The command cannot be on the front line. The command staff were on the front line, but the command itself was not there. It was in a different location. They could not be on the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the front line was at Treskavica?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I hope that answers the Chamber's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If you leave this document now, I just would like to know if the documents P1397 and P1372, they are already in evidence or are they MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I will check that for you now, Mr. President. I think they are in evidence, though. I am informed that they are in evidence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I was told that they are in evidence already. There is no need for tendering them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And what about the document 65 ter 7003, the judgement you have used?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I suppose I would tender that document. It's quite lengthy. I don't know if my -- I don't know if Mr. Gajic takes a position with respect to it, but I would tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And I take it it is not on the 65 ter exhibit list yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's not on the 65 ter list of exhibits yet, that's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence agrees for the entire judgement to be admitted as an exhibit so that not only the parts used with this witness are admitted. It contains a lot of information about the execution at Trnovo and much as been reliably established about the unit in question, and we not only do not object but fully support the tendering of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, what is your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If there is no objection to it, yes, I would tender it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received into evidence and added to the 65 ter exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P01437, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please carry on, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just before we do, we do have another witness waiting, and I know that I am a little bit over my time. My intention is to show the videotape, or some of the videotape footage. I don't know whether or not General Tolimir has cross-examination for this witness, or how extensive it is, but if perhaps Mr. Gajic could tell me, we will know whether or not, with the Court's leave, we should send the next witness home or not. I think it will take me a little while to get through the videotape and a few questions after, and he -- the witness who is waiting is an elderly man. And if we had some information, it would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir or Mr. Gajic, could you give an indication? Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence will certainly have questions for this witness. How extensive the cross-examination will be, I cannot say because this is a viva voce witness and the Prosecutor still has some questions pending. We cannot assess a duration of our cross-examination yet. In one of our submissions to the Trial Chamber, we gave a rough estimate but certainly the time we will need depends also on what the Prosecutor still wants to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In that case, this is not very probable that the we will start with the next witness. He should be released for today and come back tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to show the witness P1024, please. I think we can start, we can play some of it right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise what you see in this video footage, Mr. Stojkovic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Tell the Trial Chamber what it is.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean what it is? There are people on the truck who had been taken, I don't know from where, but they were put on a truck and they are getting ready to leave for the execution site, and Pera Petrasevic is inside. At this moment he is kicking one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And are you the one filming this particular segment of the video footage?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is this the footage that you shot, or some of the footage that you shot, having been ordered to do so by Boca, Slobodan Medic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And before you shot this video footage, is it fair to say that you knew that these men were destined to be executed by members of your unit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot state that with certainty. We did assume that, but I couldn't know for certain that they would be shot. Until the execution started, I didn't believe that they would be executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You mentioned you had a conversation with a Branislav Medic in the truck that brought them down there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What did he tell you about what was supposed to happen to the apparent cargo in that truck, meaning these men?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: He said to me that they would execute them and that these people were from Srebrenica, but I couldn't believe that would really happen. That's why I later insisted to hear who they were and where they were from, and until the execution really began, I didn't believe that it would happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: But that's what he told you; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what we see here is the footage showing the men inside the rear part of the truck?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And this is the TAM truck that you described earlier in your testimony, is it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the person that we saw before, kicking one of these men in the head, you said was whom?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Pera Petrasevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just for the record, I want the record to reflect that we played for the witness through, looks like, 21 seconds in the video. I would like to show him another segment. Hopefully we will start at 1:55. Okay. Let's play this part, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Can you stop for just a moment. We have stopped at 2 minutes, 16 seconds in the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, here we can see the men being lined up on the ground. Is that right, Mr. Stojkovic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: They have their hands behind their backs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: About how far away from these men are you when you're filming this?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Ten to 15 metres, roughly. I don't remember precisely, but thereabouts. I may have been even further away. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Or closer. Is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Or closer, possibly. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And at this point in the video --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could just continue. We will just play it through a couple more seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Stop please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the individual in the -- and we're 2 minutes, 21 seconds in the video. Do you recognise the individual in what appears to be a red beret, camouflage vest, and black coveralls, or something like that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Who is that individual?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Slobodan Davidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And he's one of the individuals that you named earlier as part of the security -- I think you said it was the security force for Slobodan Medic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. We'll play it through just a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We are at 2 minutes, 24 seconds now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And we can see here in the subtitle, it says: "Zekan, go quickly, turn the lorry around and bring it back, my battery's died." Who is saying that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the battery.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the battery of the video camera, can I assume?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when did you realise that something had -- something had gone wrong with the battery of the video camera?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: When there was the low battery signal.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And who is Zekan that you refer to here?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: That's Branislav Medic, the driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And according to your recollection, did he in fact go back to get you a new battery, or another battery?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he did. He left and came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The individuals that are in and around this area where the prisoners had been lined up, face down, on the side of the road, were they all members of your unit, that is, the Skorpions Unit, or were they members of other forces present?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand. I apologise. Could you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The individuals that were there, aside from the prisoners, in the area where they were laid down and lined up on their stomachs, were those individuals all members of your unit or were they from other units or forces in the area?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Only our unit was there. Nobody else but us. And I mean the Skorpions Unit. Nobody else was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I would like to show you P1437. That's the judgement again that I referred you to before.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And we are going to need to go to page -- yeah, let's try page 57 in the English and 46 in the B/C/S. I think we have the right pages in both. Great.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I want to refer you to, again, is what's written in the judgement about the defence of Branislav Medic, and I want to refer you to about the middle part of the paragraph in English, it will be the second paragraph, I think, in the B/C/S, and it should be around the middle of that too. In particular, what he says is: "When they all together arrived at that place, he stopped the truck and the prisoners were unloaded. He opened the tailboard so that the prisoners could get out, and when the prisoners got out of the truck, someone told them to lie down on the ground. After that, one of the Army of Republika Srpska officers, of whom he thinks that he is a lieutenant-colonel, said that he does not like this at all, that something is not right, and that he has to go back to the command. During that time, Stojkovic filmed everything. Then one of those army officers and his driver get into the Pinzgauer and drive off and the accused stays in the truck. After a few minutes, Stojkovic tells him that he should go and fetch another camera battery because this one is empty and he can't film." What I want to ask you about in particular is this apparent reference, or obvious reference, I should say, to what's written here, or translated here, is Army of Republika Srpska officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what Mr. Vanderpuye has read out I haven't seen at all. It wasn't on the screen, so probably the witness didn't see it or my legal advisor. Could we please be shown that, and only after that can the witness be asked about it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I have read, so that you can maybe reference it, follows the numbers 300 to 400 that you can see in the B/C/S. It's about seven lines down from the second -- thank you. And if we go maybe two sentences beyond that, you will see the area where I read from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you see that, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see where it says 300 to 400, but I don't see the section that Mr. Vanderpuye has read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I will read it, then, from 300 to 400 and maybe you can follow along. It says: "... which is approximately 300 to 400 metres away from the first line. He knew this place very well as he want there every day to bring food and ammo." Then the sentence: "When they all together arrived at that place ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's the beginning of that part that I just read. I will read it again: "When they all together arrived at that place, he stopped the truck, and the prisoners were unloaded. He hoped the tailboard so that the prisoners could get out, and when the prisoners got out of the truck, someone told them to lie down on the ground. After that, one of the Army of Republika Srpska officers, of whom he -" the witness - "thinks that he is a lieutenant-colonel, said that he does not like this at all, that something is not right, and he has to go back to the command. During that time Stojkovic filmed everything. Then one of those army officers and his driver get into the Pinzgauer and drive off and the accused stays with the truck. And after a few minutes, Stojkovic tells him that he should go and fetch another camera because this one is empty and he can't film."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You left out the word "battery," fetch another camera battery.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I hope -- maybe Mr. Gajic can confirm that that's actually written in the B/C/S version of it and you were able to follow along. I see Mr. Gajic is --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, now it's correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I want to ask the witness is there is a specific reference here to an Army of Republika Srpska officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could you tell us about that? Do you know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: As I was there, I can say that this didn't happen. I don't know who gave this statement, but I suppose that it was Branislav Medic, the accused. That was his version of what he said, but that doesn't match the footage because we would have been able to see these persons, otherwise. There are no outside people -- outside persons present. I mean outside persons, I mean members of the VRS around the truck. And my eyesight was good at the time and it is still good today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am not opposed to this line of questioning, but since parts of the defence of one of the accused in this trial are quoted, this should be the statement of the accused. Could Mr. Vanderpuye possibly explain to us the defence case because, given the nature of the defence case, it is clear why the person who gave this statement said what he said. I don't want to elaborate any further, but possibly Mr. Vanderpuye could enlighten us.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, first, I think that's an appropriate issue to explore on cross-examination, if General Tolimir chooses to do so. As I have done with the other questions I have put to this witness, I have asked him very simply whether or not what's recounted by a given witness or by the judge or any other circumstance comports with his recollection or understanding of the events that occurred. I am not suggesting to the witness whether one version is true or another version is not true, but this is a concrete fact which is mentioned in a judgement which concerns the presence or absence of VRS officers at the scene of an execution which is the subject of this indictment, so it's clearly relevant. What this witness knows about it as a person who was present there, obviously, and having filmed this execution, is a relevant question. He either knows or he doesn't know. He either thinks it's truthful or he doesn't think it's truthful. But I don't really see the point of my colleague's diatribe concerning the relevancy and propriety of putting questions concerning factual matters to a fact witness. And the source of the information? My good faith basis to put the question to the witness comes from a judgement which refers to that fact. Whether the judgement -- whether the Court makes that finding or not, the issue is it's a fact that is mentioned during a Court proceeding. It is perfectly appropriate to put that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I haven't put forward any objection with regard to any of the Prosecutor's questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please carry on, Mr. Vanderpuye. No, stop. Please don't carry on. We need the second break now. We will have our second break and resume quarter past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think we still had the video up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The last part of your examination was not dealing with the video but with the text you have quoted from.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that, Mr. President. I think I got an answer to my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I don't think so. There was a discussion among the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thanks, Mr. President. Just bear with me for one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, perhaps I can be of assistance. The issue that was raised was raised after the witness already replied to the question. Following that, Mr. Vanderpuye did not put any further questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Assistance is always appreciated. Thank you, Mr. Gajic. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Mr. Gajic. Just so that we are all clear, my question had to do with this reference to an Army of Republika Srpska officer that is attributed to the defence of Branislav Medic in this April 2007 judgement.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Your recollection is that all of the individuals that were at the, execution or execution site, were members of your unit. Is that correct, Mr. Stojkovic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And let me just follow up on that briefly, which is, we are talking specifically about the execution site when the camera was rolling. What about when the camera was not rolling? What about the period of time when you were not filming these events? Do you recall whether there were any officers from the Army of Republika Srpska at any point in time prior to the execution or thereafter, which is not captured on the video footage that you filmed?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, when the camera was rolling or not there was no one from the VRS, and I know this by coincidence because there were some people at the command from the VRS. That's what Medic, Branislav said when -- in his defence case. So there was no mention by him that they were at the execution site. They were at the headquarters. But I don't know whether that was the case personally because I was not -- when I arrived there, there was no one at the headquarters from the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Mindua has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, a short question for you: How many vehicles were there at the site?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do you mean; at the headquarters, the command, or at the execution site?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the execution site, how many vehicles were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only one, as I have already mentioned. It was a TAM truck, either 110 or 150 model. So there was one single vehicle, our vehicle there, there was no other vehicles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now I have a follow-up question. If I recall correctly, you have stated that somebody went back from the crime site with the truck, and later you asked Mr. Medic to go back to the headquarters to get a new battery for your video camera. Did the truck first return which went back to the headquarters and then went back again? I really don't understand this. Could you clarify that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. There was only one truck there, and Branislav Medic was the driver. I asked him to go and get a battery for the video camera for me. There was no other vehicle. And you can also see it in the footage. There were no other vehicles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think we can --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me ask you, this reference to Pinzgauer, can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: That's a military vehicle that can hold some six people in the back and two people in front, but I did not see that vehicle at any point in time, either before or after or during the incident itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Is that to say that it wasn't there or that you just didn't see one?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't there. We did not have that type of vehicle, and I can only assume that this was a statement of the accused Branislav Medic who said that there was a Pinzgauer there. It is possible that he saw it before I came there, but I cannot really claim that with certainty that there was that vehicle there. Other people claim that it wasn't. And I, myself, cannot say that it was when I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, we turn back to the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I want to play it from a different point. Okay. We are at 3 minutes, 49 seconds in the video, and we can just play it through a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us first, Mr. Stojkovic, who are the individuals that we have just seen in the frames through -- we have stopped now at 3 minutes and 55 seconds?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: The person we see now is Aleksandar Medic, and the other three were Pera Petrasevic, Davidovic, and Momic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And these are all members of your unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. We can continue playing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, you see here a reference to one of the men asking somebody if they have fucked, if you excuse my language, but that's what's attributed to them. Do you recall that part of the footage?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And who said that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I think either Aleksandar Medic or Davidovic. I don't know exactly who it was who put the question, I think it was Davidovic, and that Aleksandar Medic commented in response.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you know why -- well, first of all, whom this soldier was talking to?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: He was actually talking to one of the prisoners who are lying down on the floor, but basically he asked him whether he had had any love relationship, and he said that he didn't, and that's basically what they were commenting on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could play through a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. We can stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, we just heard a sound. Hopefully you heard it too. Could you tell us what that was?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Perhaps if we could replay it then I could pay attention to such matters. Maybe there was -- maybe a shot was fired. I think there was a shot fired while there was this conversation going on, but I couldn't hear it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you have a recollection of a shot being fired - let my put it to you that way - during this part of the footage that you were filming?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, could you replay it? Maybe there was a shell fired, I don't know, but I know that while earlier on, as they were talking, this Momic person, he pulled out his rifle and he fired into the air, but maybe there was also a shell being fired. I don't know. But it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, this conversation that we saw part of in the subtitles of this footage where you recall that it had something to do with whether or not one of the prisoners had had some love, I think you said, it was part of your testimony, was it not, in Belgrade, and in particular I will refer you to your 23rd February 2006 testimony. Do you remember having testified about that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recall being asked this question and giving these answers, I should say, by the Presiding Judge in those proceedings? Now, I can refer you to page 73 and 74 in the English. I am not sure -- it's 65 ter 7005, but for the purposes, it should be page 38 in the B/C/S, but I will just read it to you and ask you if it refreshes your recollection. If you need to see it, then I will show it to you. It reads as follows. You were asked: "What did he ask them? So it doesn't matter. We hear all sorts of things here. You must tell us what you heard regardless of what it is and what words were used." That's the judge. Your answer: "I am really embarrassed." "Q. There is no need to be embarrassed. We are used to everything here. Nothing is embarrassing here." "A. Well, as far as I -- last time, as far as I understood what he was asking, and you can also hear that in the recording, he is asking him, the last one on the right --" "Q. The one next to you, who was the first one next to you?" "A. He asked the one next to me. That's why you can hear what I asked him." "What did he ask him?" "He asked: 'Did you fuck?'" "Q. All right." "A. And he said no, and Aca told him, 'And you won't either,' something like that, but I am not sure if I phrased it exactly, but it was something to that effect." Do you recall giving that testimony as concerns what we just saw here in the video footage?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember making such a statement. And I also attended a new trial when Aleksandar Medic was there, and when we listened to the video, I heard it and I believe that's what I said exactly, that's what I remember, and I am not trying to hide anything now but not everything was written down as I said then. Now, the new trial was actually a retrial because it was referred back by the Appeals Chamber to the initial -- to the original Trial Chamber and this is what I recall that was said, and I recall that something to the effect of, "Well, if you haven't fucked around anymore anyway," although, in retrospect, I am not sure that that's what I said, but it is possible. And obviously I couldn't remember, ten years later, every single word, and in that trial I had not seen the video footage before I was asked that question and I answered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, the gist of my question is, when you say that Aca told him, "And you won't either," did you understand that to mean that that individual was going to be executed and he would never have that chance?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I just explained that the context was not exactly as it was just presented here. That was not what was said. So there was a completely different understanding of it, however it would probably make sense that it went on where he would have said that, well, if you haven't, then you won't have a chance to do it again, and then it would be a logical extension of that that he won't because he would be shot. But as I said, when I went back for that retrial we were trying to determine what was said exactly and that's what I said because that is what I remembered, that is how I remembered it. But when I testified the first time before the Special Chamber in Belgrade, it was the case that I had not seen the video footage beforehand, and I did not have it in my own possession, and I didn't really -- couldn't really recollect everything that was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. It is your testimony, though, that at this point when these prisoners were lined up face down on the side of the road, that you still didn't believe that they were going to be executed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I could not understand it to mean that he would kill them, because I didn't believe what they were saying, that there would be an execution, because that's how it usually happened. And I thought that there would be an exchange. Because all of this was happening in the context of stories about either an exchange or execution, but as far as I could see now it was really an execution. But up until the last moment, I didn't know, and I didn't believe that they would execute them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we can go to the next segment we are going to play.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just before we play that, let me ask you, when you first saw these prisoners in the back of the truck, it was clear to you that they had been beaten up; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that would be normal, from your point of view, with respect to an exchange to be carried out with these prisoners. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know, as I sit here, whether it was normal or not, or it would be normal or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let's take a look at what we have here. We're at 16 minutes, 8 seconds, in the video footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think we can stop now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Tell us what we see here. What you are filming?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, here I was filming the part where the execution had already been carried out and four others were left to pull the bodies over to the summer cottages.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, I haven't shown you the entirety of this video footage, but did you shoot more footage than what I have shown you here in court?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: You mean on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, on this occasion, with respect to the executions that were carried out against these Muslim men from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there is more footage than this.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And of the video footage that I've shown you now, in court, is there anything in the video footage that you did not record?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Everything that you showed, I recorded myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is it accurate to your recollection of the events that actually transpired on the day that you were filming these killings?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you, since you've indicated that you didn't believe that these men were to be executed, I just want to ask you one other question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We should indicate that you stopped the video at 16 minutes, 18 seconds -- 18.4 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. I appreciate that. That's P1437. I need page 27 in the English and page 27 in the B/C/S. Again, we are back to the April 2007 judgement. And this is what's in the judgement as concerns Pera Petrasevic, his defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you will tell me if you can find this in the B/C/S because I am not sure which paragraph it is, but it reads: "That morning (before they would head out to perform the task) --" It looks like it's -- that's right, the first paragraph, the first complete paragraph on that page. "-- someone woke him up and hold him 'Come down, aka Boca needs you.'" That would be Slobodan Medic, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: "He got up, looked down the staircase and saw Slobodan Medic who addressed him with the words, 'Come down, I have a task for you all.' The accused understood - that would be Petrasevic - that there was a task for the members of the security, which meant him, Milorad Momic, Aleksandar Medic, and Slobodan Davidovic. I came down and saw some ten to 15 people standing around a truck. Among them, he remembers that Slobodan Stojkovic was standing at the corner of the weekend house." First, do you remember standing at the corner of the weekend house at any point in time prior to the executions that we've seen in the video footage? Do you recall that, Mr. Stojkovic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, but it doesn't match. I arrived last. They had already gotten off and gotten ready and they were only waiting for me. But apart from that, the context is all right, is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Further to what I have just read, Petrasevic, at least what appears to be attributed to him, says he: "... came down, saw ten to 15 people standing around the truck. Among them he remembers Slobodan Stojkovic was standing at the corner of the weekend house," as I've just read. "Then Slobodan Medic addressed the accused Petrasevic with the words, 'Go and kill these people.' At that moment nobody else was in his vicinity, but he is certain that Slobodan Stojkovic could also hear these words." Do you have a recollection of that order being issued by Boca with regard to these men that you filmed being executed in or around Trnovo in the video footage?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: After you filmed this video footage, could you tell us what you did with it.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: When I returned to Djeletovci, I asked the commander what I should do with that video cassette, and the commander ordered me to give it to Kosanovic - what's his name again? - we called him Kosa, I don't remember his first name now. And I gave it to him, the video cassette, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you say "that's it," what do you mean? Do you know what happened to the video cassette after you gave it to him?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I later heard that the -- that several copies were made and that they distributed it among themselves. Some of them had it. And Dusko Kosanovic - I remember his name now, Dusko - he kept a copy, and I also heard that a copy was available for rent at the video store at Sid. I don't know if that's true. But allegedly whoever wanted could go there and rent the cassette and see the footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Stojkovic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, for indulging. I know that I am over my limit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed. At this point in time I would like to put three questions to the witness just to clarify some matters. On page 34 of today's transcript, line 9, you said: "Dusko Kosanovic had the camera before me and he accompanied the unit and all he did was record, but then he had some psychological problems. He was returned to Djeletovci, probably couldn't bear everything that was happening there, and the camera stayed behind whereas he went to Djeletovci." Can you tell us something about the psychological problems you were referring to of this man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know exactly what he experienced, but I heard from other people that he was scared of the events there because we were shelled heavily. But I wasn't in contact with him, I heard it from others. Anyway, he was sent back and his statement was that he fell ill. I don't know. It may be true. At any rate, he was sent back to Djeletovci, or, rather, he went home. He wasn't a member of the Skorpions. He only accompanied us when video recordings were to be made. Only when we were out in the field, then he would come with us and film, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Was he at any point in time present at the execution site of these six men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, he wasn't. He can't have been. He was at home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What do you mean when you said: "Probably he couldn't bear everything that was happening there"? What, in your understanding, was the problem he was suffering from? "What was happening there," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to say that probably the man was scared of getting killed. He couldn't bear it, because many people got killed and he was probably unable to stand it. That's my conclusion. Maybe I am wrong. Maybe he really fell ill, but I do believe that my assumption is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Another question: You several times today stated that you didn't believe that these six men were from Srebrenica, although you were told they came from there. Why didn't you believe that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't believe it because it was impossible. As far as I know, Srebrenica was over 200 kilometres away from the place where we were and I didn't understand how they could possibly have come there. They would have needed two or three days to reach us, and that's why I didn't think it possible for them to be able to come to the place where we were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And why did you want to know and to ask them if they are really from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly because I didn't believe that they were from Srebrenica. I wanted to find out where they were from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What would be the difference if these men were from Srebrenica or from any other place, the difference for you in the understanding of the event you were involved in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, from today's vantage point, it would have made a difference, but at the time I was just curious to know where they were from. I didn't know then what was happening in Srebrenica. However, today, I know more about the events around Srebrenica. I don't know exactly what happened, but generally speaking, I do know now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That was not precisely what I was asking you. I would like to know what was your understanding at that time when you wanted to find out if they were really from Srebrenica. Was it at that point in time your understanding that there was difference -- would be a difference if they would be from another location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know how to answer that question. I really don't know. I was just curious to know where they were from. It didn't make a difference to me whether they were from Srebrenica or another place, Sarajevo or any other place, it meant nothing to me at the time. I didn't know what was happening at Srebrenica, why it was so topical; I didn't know anything at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And my third question is related to a part of the video we have seen. You were asked by Mr. Vanderpuye about the man with the name Zekan, and you said that's Branislav Medic. And --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- you asked him to go back and to bring you a new battery because your battery was empty; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Was he superior to you or was he your subordinate? What was your relation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't his superior and he wasn't my superior, either. We were both equal soldiers, but I simply had to tell someone that my battery had died and that another had to be brought. There was no superior of mine present, nor was I superior to anybody else; I couldn't give anybody orders. I understood that Pera Petrasevic was superior to everybody else there. That's what I understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: How long did you wait for the return of the truck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ten to 15 minutes, maybe. I can't remember exactly, but thereabouts. The distance is 4 kilometres, so it would have certainly taken ten to 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What happened in that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing. The camera was in use at the time, save [Realtime transcript read in error "say"] for 4 to 5 minutes, but nothing much happened. Only people talked and whatever was said was recorded. Nothing much happened. We only waited for the battery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sorry. I didn't understand that. You said the camera was in use all the time. I was only referring to the time when you waited for the return of the truck with the new battery. Was the camera in use at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've just said that it wasn't in use all the time. Four or five minutes it was not in use, but it wasn't really in operation the entire time. When the truck returned, then it was put back to use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And what was the reason that you waited for the return of the truck? And I mean the whole group, why did they wait and started the execution after the return of the truck and not earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because it couldn't be filmed, but everybody knew that it must be filmed. They knew of the commander's orders to film it. That's why we waited and that's why everything went the way it went.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, you were on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, I was, Mr. President, and only because a clarification or correction should be made to the transcript. I have as page 79, line 12, which is attributed to the witness as having said: "The camera was in use all the time," and then it reads, "Say for 45 minutes," and I think it should read "save for four to five minutes," which I think ultimately was corrected by the witness further down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I said that it may have been out of use for four minutes or five, to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that clarification. Mr. Tolimir, it was not possible to commence your cross-examination today because of my questions I had to put to the witness. It is now 7.00, we have to adjourn for the day, and are you in the position to commence your cross-examination tomorrow? Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Mr. Vanderpuye asked whether we would finish. I don't know what the commitments of this witness are or what the plan is. Since you have asked many questions and so has he, it will suffice for my legal advisor to read the conclusions of the Belgrade judgement which will provide many answers to these questions, and they spent two years investigating this. And it is only one paragraph. If you allow, we can do it now and then we can release the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That is the only question you want to put? But there will be probably or possibly re-examination. Mr. Vanderpuye, do you know anything about the preparations for the return of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I am afraid I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In my view it is better to adjourn for the day to give you the possibility to prepare your cross-examination during the break, and then we will resume tomorrow. And I heard from Judges that there are additional questions. I think we shouldn't hurry it because we are over time already. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what Mr. Tolimir wanted is in evidence already, but we wanted to read it out for the sake of the record, but at present we have no questions for the witness. We only wanted to read out one paragraph from the judgement that is already in evidence. That would not be a question, nor would the witness be in a position to reply to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The witness should be available tomorrow and maybe we can ask him. That's point one. Point two is if they don't have any questions, then they don't have any questions, but I don't really see the point of reading out a document which isn't a question because then it's not a proper examination of the witness in any event. So it's one or the other, but in any event I think that the witness will be here tomorrow, I think that we are all aware of the circumstances under which he is here, and that's something squarely within the control of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have just consulted Mr. Tolimir. We have no questions for this witness. What we wanted to do we can also do tomorrow or we can make a written submission or we can do it in our final statement. It makes no difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That means you have no cross-examination for the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe has a final question for the witness -- sorry, Judge Mindua. It's too late now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well it is late, and I only have four short questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, do you know why your commander wanted footage of the execution? Very briefly, please, because I also have other questions.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you would have to ask him probably. As far as I know, he wanted them as a souvenir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. My second question would be to ask you about your feelings when you were requested to film this execution. Did you feel that you were carrying out an important official task for the army or were you just making -- doing a personal service to your commander?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, I carried out orders. I don't know what to tell you now about my feelings at the moment. It was long ago. I can't remember how I felt at that moment. It's been over 15 years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you know that you're doing somebody a service, for example, when the commander asks for a cigarette, that's not a military thing, that's a pure favour, but my third question is: The participants distributed copies among themselves. If I understood correctly, these are souvenirs?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why do you think did he collect those copies?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. What kind of copies? Dusko Kosanovic personally made a copy and brought him the cassette for him to have as a souvenir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, because the cassette that was copied as a souvenir was distributed to other participants, so it was meant to be a souvenir. That was the reason of it being distributed to all the participants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. Was this a question or a comment? I apologise. Could you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said that copies of your cassette were distributed to all the participants in the execution. For what reason was that done? Was it to give everybody a personal souvenir or did it have a military purpose?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I can only state my opinion. I don't know what they wanted to achieve. I believe that it was meant to be a souvenir of the war, of the combat. I don't know. I didn't receive one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And my last question is: On page 75, line 20 of the transcript, you said that: "Everybody could borrow a copy from the video store at Sid." What kind of video store was that? Was it a public video store or was it a military facility?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, it was just a regular video store, just like here in The Hague or any other town. You go there, you rent a video cassette, pay a fee, and return it after two or three days, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sir, you will be pleased to hear that this concludes your examination of today. The Chamber would like to thank you that you came here, and now you are free to return to your normal activities. As there was no cross-examination, there was no re-examination, and all of a sudden this part is over. Thank you very much again and goodbye. And we have to adjourn. First of all I have to express my apologies for the staff again, I think it is the third time this week that we are over time. My apologies, and I would like to express my gratitude for the patience of all the staff. Thank you very much. We adjourn and resume tomorrow in the afternoon at 2.15 in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: 7.10 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 2nd day of December, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.
